title: COMBIN 6 of 16 on the discriminating capture, on the shipped multiply-first loop
status_plain: A cycle-2 design-for-divergence capture put 16 discriminating (n, k) pairs with representable results against Excel and found that Excel matches OxFunc's multiply-first form only 6 of 16 times; ratio-first scores 2 of 16, exact-integer 6 of 16, and neither 8 of 16. Excel sits 1 to 3 ULP BELOW the multiply-first product at larger n and k. The multiply-first form named in that sentence, (acc*(n-k+i))/i, is verbatim what OxFunc ships: combinatorics_common.rs::combinations_of_int reduces k to min(k, n-k) and then loops acc *= (n-k+i) followed by acc /= i. So 6 of 16 is a PRODUCTION count, not a refutation of a candidate. It also corrected an earlier over-claim: a cycle-1 "bit-exact below 2^53" claim rested on a non-discriminating 7-point corpus where every form agrees below about 2^40, and it is now recorded as disproven. Every plain-double and x87-prec64 product ordering scores the same 6 of 16, so the residual is an op-graph question, not an accumulation-order one, and the row stays open.

The catalogue names the leading hypothesis for Excel as an internal extended lgamma/exp substrate, and points at the PERMUT x87 spill-product family (closed at 702/702) as the substrate to race against.
ruled_out: All product-loop, factorial-ratio, reciprocal-multiply and published-GAMMALN-composition kernels, on a 505-row live corpus.
x87-prec64 product orderings — every ordering, double and x87 alike, scores 6 of 16.
